title: Affine subgroup generated by an inverse-stable pointed map
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $G$ an affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $X$ an affine $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] of finite type. Fix a $k$-point $o$ of $X$ [def-pc-rational-point] and a $k$-morphism $\varphi:X\to G$ with $\varphi(o)=e$. Assume that for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$, the subset $\varphi(X(R))\subseteq G(R)$ is stable under inversion. For $n\geq1$ define $w_n:X^n\to G$ by $w_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=\varphi(x_1)\cdots\varphi(x_n)$, with powers formed over $k$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $A=k[G]$, $I_n=\ker(w_n^*:A\to k[X^n])$ and $I=\bigcap_{n\geq1}I_n$, using affine coordinate algebras and quotient rings [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Then $L=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, with its canonical closed immersion into $G$, is a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup], and $\varphi$ factors through $L$. For every closed subgroup scheme $K\subseteq G$ through which $\varphi$ factors, $L\subseteq K$. The scheme $L$ is affine of finite type. If $X$ is geometrically reduced, then $L$ is geometrically reduced; if $X$ is geometrically connected, then $L$ is geometrically connected, with these terms as in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Propositions 2.46 and 2.48, printed pp.54–55 (affine construction and geometric reducedness/connectedness)

proof.text: Write $B_n=k[X^n]$, $C=A/I$ and $q:A\to C$. The maps $x\mapsto(x,o)$ give $w_{n+1}(x,o)=w_n(x)$, hence $I_{n+1}\subseteq I_n$. Since $I\subseteq I_n$, the formula $f_n(q(a))=w_n^*(a)$ defines a $k$-algebra map $f_n:C\to B_n$. These maps jointly detect zero: if all $f_n(q(a))$ vanish, then $a\in\bigcap_n I_n=I$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], $\operatorname{Spec}q$ is a closed immersion, and $\varphi=w_1$ factors through it because $I\subseteq I_1$.

Let $\Delta:A\to A\otimes_k A$ be pullback by multiplication; the affine product identifications are [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]. For $a\in I$, put $t=(q\otimes q)\Delta(a)\in C\otimes_k C$. The word identity $m\circ(w_n\times w_m)=w_{n+m}$ gives $(f_n\otimes f_m)(t)=w_{n+m}^*(a)=0$ for every $n,m\geq1$. Fix $n$. Apply [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection] to the family $f_m:C\to B_m$ and right factor $B_n$, after swapping the two factors of $(f_n\otimes\mathrm{id}_C)(t)$. It is killed by every $f_m\otimes\mathrm{id}_{B_n}$, so it is zero. Apply that node once more to the family $f_n$ and right factor $C$: $t=0$. Thus $(q\otimes q)\Delta$ kills $I$ and descends to $C\to C\otimes_kC$.

For $a\in I$ we have $a(e)=w_1^*(a)(o)=0$, so the identity map on points factors through $L$. Let $S:A\to A$ be pullback by inversion. For fixed $n$, use $R=B_n$ and the universal tuple $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\in X^n(R)$. Inversion stability supplies $y_i\in X(R)$ with $\varphi(y_i)=\varphi(x_i)^{-1}$. Consequently $w_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n)^{-1}=w_n(y_n,\ldots,y_1)$. Since $w_n^*(a)=0$, evaluation at this latter tuple is zero; this says $w_n^*(S(a))=0$ in $B_n$. This holds for every $n$, hence $S(I)\subseteq I$. The counit and inverse therefore descend to $C$. Along with the multiplication of step 2 they give $L$ the restricted group operations. Their group identities hold because their images in $G(R)$ do, and $L(R)\to G(R)$ is injective for every $R$ (a map from $A/I$ is determined by its composite with $q$). Thus $L$ is a closed subgroup in the pointwise definition [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup].

Let $K\subseteq G$ be a closed subgroup through which $\varphi$ factors. Since $G$ is affine, [def-weil-closed-immersion] writes $K=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)$ for an ideal $J$. Its subgroup multiplication shows that every $w_n$ factors through $K$, hence $J\subseteq I_n$ for every $n$ and $J\subseteq I$. The map $A/J\to A/I$, $a+J\mapsto a+I$, exhibits $L\subseteq K$. Finally, $A$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs], applied to the finite-type structure morphism $G\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ with the affine opens $U=G$ and $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and a finite set of $k$-algebra generators of $A$ maps to generators of $C$. Thus $L=\operatorname{Spec}C$ is affine of finite type, as required.

Fix any field extension $K/k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra], the coordinate rings of $L_K$ and $(X^n)_K$ are $C_K=C\otimes_kK$ and $B_{n,K}=B_n\otimes_kK$; the base-changed word maps have pullbacks $f_{n,K}=f_n\otimes\mathrm{id}_K$. By [lem-sfb-vector-space-tensor-family-zero-detection], these maps jointly detect zero, since the $f_n$ do. The point $e$ of $L$ from step 3 gives $e_K\in L_K(K)$, and each word map carries $(o_K,\ldots,o_K)$ to $e_K$. We will detect nilpotents and idempotents in $C_K$ by the maps $f_{n,K}$.

source.place: Proposition 2.47 and proof of Proposition 2.48, printed p.55

proof.text: Assume $X$ geometrically reduced. Then $X_K$ is geometrically reduced for every $K/k$, directly from the quantifier over all field extensions in [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The finite products $(X_K)^n$ are reduced by induction: the base $n=1$ is the hypothesis; use [lem-sfb-flat-geometrically-reduced-pullback] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$, $Y=X_K$, $T=(X_K)^n$ for the induction step. Here $Y\to S$ is flat by [lem-pc-flat-field], and its field fibres are reduced by geometric reducedness. The coordinate ring $k[X]$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] (the affine opens $U=X$ over $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ of the finite-type structure morphism), so the coordinate ring $B_n\otimes_kK$ of $T$ is finitely generated over $K$ (tensor products are generated by the generators of their factors), hence Noetherian by [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components]; the single affine chart $T$ then makes $T$ locally Noetherian in the sense of [pqf-def-locnoeth], as that pullback lemma requires. Thus every $B_{n,K}$ is reduced. Any nilpotent $z\in C_K$ maps to zero in every $B_{n,K}$, and step 5 gives $z=0$. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme], $L_K$ is reduced. Since $K$ was arbitrary, $L$ is geometrically reduced.

source.place: Proposition 2.48, printed p.55; reduced-product input: Stacks Tag 035Z, varieties.tex, lemma-geometrically-reduced-any-base-change; the cited flat pullback lemma gives the same input

proof.text: Assume $X$ geometrically connected. For every $K/k$, $X_K$ is geometrically connected by the same field-extension quantifier. Inductively $(X_K)^n$ is connected: [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] identifies the components of $X_K\times_K (X_K)^{n-1}$ with those of $(X_K)^{n-1}$. The powers are nonempty because they contain the tuple of copies of $o_K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], each $B_{n,K}$ has only the idempotents $0,1$. If $z\in C_K$ is idempotent, every $f_{n,K}(z)$ is $0$ or $1$, and evaluation at $(o_K,\ldots,o_K)$ shows that its value is always the same scalar $z(e_K)\in\{0,1\}$. Thus all $f_{n,K}$ kill $z-z(e_K)1$, and step 5 implies $z=z(e_K)1$. Again by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], $L_K$ has no nontrivial clopen decomposition; it is nonempty by $e_K$, so is connected. For all $K/k$ this gives geometric connectedness.
